study_type_evidence.section: RESULTS / Pharmacokinetics of MS~[Gln6,14]CNP-38 Conjugates 4A and 4B

study_type_evidence.quote: Groups of 3-wk-old wild-type mice (n = 6) were given daily subcutaneous administrations of 70 nmol/kg CNP variants or vehicle for 5 wk.
When assayed in the 3T3 cell NPR-B guanylate cyclase assay, [Gln6,14]CNP-38 showed a half maximal effective concentration (EC50) of 3 nM compared with 11 nM for vosoritide

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: adult CD1 mice (pharmacokinetic studies); sex and age not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Pharmacokinetic studies of 4A and 4B were not assessed in juvenile mice because of anticipated difficulties in analysis of long-acting prodrugs in rapidly growing animals.
in_vivo_species.section: RESULTS / Pharmacokinetics of MS~[Gln6,14]CNP-38 Conjugates 4A and 4B

in_vivo_species.quote: Using 3-wk-old ∼15-g FVB/nJ male mice, we studied the growth stimulatory effects of various regimens of 4A and 4B
Pharmacokinetics in the cyno monkey and simulations in humans (SI Appendix Fig. S5 and S6) suggest that the [Gln6,14]CNP-38 released from 4A should remain in the therapeutic window
in_vivo_species.section: RESULTS / Estimations of Human Equivalent Doses of 4A and 4B

in_vitro_detail: 3T3 cell NPR-B guanylate cyclase (cGMP) assay for EC50 determination; HPLC-monitored chemical stability/deamidation of vosoritide, CNP-38 and [Gln6,14]CNP-38 in buffer at pH 7.4 and 37 C over 4 wk; protein L-isoaspartyl methyltransferase (PIMT) assay to detect isoAsp formation; in vitro beta-eliminative linker release kinetics from the microsphere conjugates at pH 9.4 and 37 C extrapolated to pH 7.4.

notes: The Materials and Methods section of the body is a single paragraph that defers everything to the SI Appendix ('In vitro kinetic procedures are provided as are in vivo pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic methods and analyses'), so the ELISA and LC-MS/MS assays listed in the PeplLife2 metadata are NOT described anywhere in the body; bioanalytical_method is therefore recorded as not reported. Group size for the pharmacokinetic study is likewise absent; the only n in the body is n = 6 for the Fig. 2 growth comparison. Amino acid sequences are presented only as an image in Fig. 1, so no one-letter sequence could be taken from the body; the PeplLife2 sequence LQEHPQARKYKGAQKKGLSKGCFGLKLDRIGSMSGLGC does not appear as text in the body. The four PeplLife2 half-life rows map exactly onto the body values: 4A t1/2,alpha ~40 h and t1/2,beta ~212 h; 4B t1/2,alpha ~60 h and t1/2,beta ~610 h, all in adult CD1 mouse plasma. Note the body reports two different sets of in vitro linker release half-lives at pH 7.4/37 C: 600 h (4A) and 1,580 h (4B) in the Results, versus 185 h (4A) and 1,200 h (4B) in the Discussion - this discrepancy is in the source text and has not been resolved. The reported Cmax and Cmin values for 4A and 4B are SIMULATED/predicted from the fitted PK, not directly observed; this is stated explicitly ('Assuming dose linearity, simulations for conjugate 4A indicated...'). Cynomolgus monkey pharmacokinetics are referred to in the body but the data appear only in SI Appendix Figs. S5 and S6. Cumulative 4-week doses per mouse are tabulated in Table 1: 44 nmol for QD [Gln6,14]CNP-38, 80 nmol for QWk 4A 20 nmol/mouse, 132 nmol for QWk 4A 1.5 umol/kg, 86 nmol for Q2Wk 4A 2.2 umol/kg, and 95 nmol for QMo 4B 6.1 umol/kg.
